uncited: *   **Fringe Data:** Digital representation of the holographic phase/amplitude.
*   **RF Signal:** High-frequency analog signal derived from the fringe data, driving the AOM.
**Fringe Computation:** Compute the holographic fringes for the desired 3D scene.
**Digital-to-Analog Conversion:** Convert the digitally computed fringes into high-frequency analog electrical signals.
**Acoustic Wave Generation:** The analog RF signal is applied to the transducer of an AOM crystal.
**Phase Modulation:** A beam of laser light passes through the AOM.
The acoustic wave phase-modulates the light beam.
**Horizontal Scanning:** A rapidly moving mirror (scanning system) angularly multiplexes the image of the modulated light.
**Visual Integration:** The human eye, with a latency of typically 20 ms, time-integrates the rapidly scanned light.

The scanning process is hardware-accelerated by the optical system and human integration.
*   **When to Use:** When large volume holographic imagery is required and hardware complexity/cost is not a primary constraint.
*   **When Not to Use:** When low-cost, easily interfaced digital displays (LCD/DMD) are sufficient, or when real-time computation of large fringes is not feasible.
